new_findings_today.title: RESOLVED: the '405→186 local_helpers drop' was apples-to-oranges. 405 = destinations.deep_dive.local_helpers (intact: still 405 blocks / 867 entries today); 186 = emergency_sos.local_helpers (a DIFFERENT, always-sparse column). new_findings_today.detail: Two distinct fields were conflated across runs. (1) destinations.deep_dive->'local_helpers' is the curated phone-bearing helper list the QA harness measured on 2026-06-04..06-07 — the findings literally name the metric 'deep_dive.local_helpers'. (2) emergency_sos.local_helpers is a SEPARATE table column holding sparser, often phone-less informal helpers. LIVE DB TODAY: destinations.deep_dive ? 'local_helpers' = 405 rows, all non-empty arrays, 867 total entries — an EXACT match to the historical '405 blocks / 867 phone entries'. So the 405 source is 100% intact and unchanged. The 186 I measured today is emergency_sos.local_helpers non-empty — a different column that has always been sparse, and whose 186 holders are a STRICT SUBSET of the 405 deep_dive holders. Today's Section-E probe silently re-pointed from deep_dive.local_helpers to emergency_sos.local_helpers, then compared the new field's 186 against the old field's carried-forward 405 → a phantom 219-row 'loss' that never happened. constants-reverify-2026-06-09 is fully exonerated: migration 069 only creates a staleness-classifier VIEW (reads local_police_station/nearest_hospital), and the reverify only stamped verified_date/last_verified_attempt_at/verified_by — it never UPDATEs any local_helpers array (proven in data/audits/sos-reverify-2026-06-09.md). emergency_sos.updated_at being stuck at 2026-06-04 is real (the table has no auto-update trigger) but irrelevant here — no helper data changed.
new_findings_today.evidence: DB (dudzsdzfvikjjhurxrgc): destinations.deep_dive?'local_helpers' = 405 present / 405 nonempty / 0 empty / 867 total entries (== historical 405/867, exact). emergency_sos.local_helpers nonempty = 186, all within the 405 deep_dive holders (overlap 186). jaipur proof of two datasets: deep_dive.local_helpers = 3 phoned helplines (Rajasthan Tourism 0141-5110598 / Police 100 / Dial 112); emergency_sos.local_helpers = 2 phone-less descriptive helpers (Hawa Mahal tourist police booth / hotel concierge). new_findings_today.recommendation: NO restore required — no data was lost. Harness fix: pin daily Section-E to the fields the SITE actually renders — confidence_cards.people_who_help (491/525, the 'People who help' card via confidence-card.tsx) and emergency_sos.local_helpers (186/525, the SOS sub-section via emergency-sos.tsx) — and STOP measuring destinations.deep_dive.local_helpers, which is an unrendered legacy/backing store (no component reads it). An updated_at trigger on emergency_sos remains a nice-to-have for dating future changes.

new_findings_today.title: Harness artifact: probe SW-version regex grabs nakshiq-v32 from the cleanup list; actual CACHE_VERSION is v51 (file byte-identical 7 days)
new_findings_today.detail: probe.py sec_g uses re.search(r'nakshiq-v\d+', body), which returns the FIRST match. sw.js contains a cache-cleanup/delete list enumerating old names (v32,v33,…,v50) before the active const CACHE_VERSION = "nakshiq-v51". So the probe mislabels the active SW as v32. md5 of /sw.js is d0cc522e363cd7fc6521684ac6679f9a — byte-identical to 2026-06-07 (and the 6 days before), so the SW is unchanged (now 7 consecutive identical days). No service-worker regression; purely a harness extraction bug.
new_findings_today.evidence: grep on /sw.js: 'const CACHE_VERSION = "nakshiq-v51' present; 15 nakshiq-v* strings v32..v51; md5 d0cc522e363cd7fc6521684ac6679f9a (15144 bytes).
new_findings_today.recommendation: Patch probe.py sec_g to anchor: re.search(r'CACHE_VERSION\s*=\s*"(nakshiq-v\d+)"', body) (fall back to max nakshiq-v<N>). One-line fix; harness only.
